newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end up sharply on mill curtailments.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end up sharply on mill curtailments.

text.p: CME lumber futures shot up the $10.00 per tbf daily limit early and closed sharply higher on talk a major Canadian lumber producer would be curtailing production, traders said.

Confirmation of the rumor did not come until after the close, and some traders took quick profits and pare the limit gain. But futures remained strong on the expected cutback in production, traders said.
Slocan Forest Products Ltd of Canada said Thursday afternoon that it plans to reduce lumber production through temporary shutdowns at about 10 sawmills in August.
CME lumber closed $1.50 to $9.50 per tbf higher with September up $7.00 at $343.70 after being up limit earlier at $346.70 per tbf. November ended up $6.40 at $340.70 per tbf.
Cash market sources estimated the Slocan cutback would amount to 30 million to 35 million board feet which Slocan's Chief Financial Officer Ron Price said was "reasonable".

But traders said the overall effect of the Slocan move and some other mill curtailments may have only limited effect on the market if demand for wood does not increase. Home sales are running less than expected even with low interest rates, they said.
"They're not shutting down (mills) because business is great," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
